title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
prompt: Given two integers `left` and `right` that represent the range `[left, right]`, return the bitwise AND of all numbers in this range, inclusive.
hints: ANDing a huge range of numbers one by one would be too slow for large ranges — look for a pattern instead.

As soon as two numbers in the range differ in a bit position, ANDing across the full range zeroes that position out (since some number in between will have a 0 there). So only the common binary prefix shared by left and right survives.
Repeatedly right-shift both left and right by 1, counting the shifts, until they become equal. That common prefix, shifted back left by the shift count, is the answer.

solution.approach: The bitwise AND of every number in [left, right] can only keep the bits that are identical across the entire range; any bit position where numbers in the range differ will be zeroed by some intermediate value, since incrementing through a range flips lower bits before higher ones. So repeatedly shift both left and right one bit to the right, counting the shifts, until they become equal — that common value is the shared binary prefix. Shifting it back left by the same count restores it to the correct bit positions and zeroes out everything that wasn't shared.
solution.code:
def range_bitwise_and(left, right):
    shift = 0
    while left < right:
        left >>= 1
        right >>= 1
        shift += 1
    return left << shift
